site_name: QTS Ashburn-Shellhorn (ASH3) campus, 22271 Shellhorn Road, Ashburn, VA 20147
year_evidence_quote: QTS broke ground on the Shellhorn project on June 1, 2020, and completed the space with fully-commissioned power in place on Dec. 31.
year_site_match: Article names 'Shellhorn DC-1' / 'Ashburn-Shellhorn' in Ashburn, Virginia, 310,000 sq ft, 42 MW. QTS's own Ashburn 3 (ASH3) page lists 'ASH3 DC1: 22291 Shellhorn Rd Ashburn, VA 20147' and 'ASH3 DC2: 22271 Shellhorn Rd Ashburn, VA 20147', so the record address (22271) is DC2 and the campus's first building is DC1 next door. EPA registry row 'ASH3 - Ashburn- Shellhorn DC1' shows floor space 310388, matching the article's 310,000 sq ft.
verification: Medium, not high, for two reasons. (1) The article does not print a year next to 'Dec. 31'; 2020 follows from the June 1, 2020 groundbreaking plus the same article's 'from dirt to a fully-commissioned data center in seven months'. The article also says Shellhorn DC-1 was cited as Construction Project of the Year in the Northern Virginia Technology Council's 2021 Data Center Awards, which fits a 2020 completion. (2) Unresolved conflict: the EPA ENERGY STAR registry gives year constructed 2022 for both Shellhorn DC1 and DC2. I could not find a third page to settle it; my inference (not verified) is the EPA DC1 value is a self-reported entry error or reflects a later phase. The article states commissioning, not a customer move-in date, and Dec. 31 sits on the 2020/2021 boundary, so first customer load may have been early 2021. Address 22271 is the second building (DC2); the 2020 date is for DC1 at 22291. The cited DCF article gives no street address. A Data Center Dynamics URL I tried returned 403.

lead.year_evidence_quote: QTS broke ground on the Shellhorn project on June 1, 2020, and completed the space with fully-commissioned power in place on Dec. 31.
lead.notes: DCF (April 13, 2022) says QTS broke ground on Shellhorn on June 1, 2020 and completed it with fully commissioned power on Dec. 31, 'dirt to a fully-commissioned data center in seven months'. That puts completion at Dec. 31, 2020, but the year comes from the arithmetic, not a stated date, hence medium. Directories place DC2 at 22271 and DC1 next door at 22291 Shellhorn, so the campus's first building is DC1. Conflict: the EPA ENERGY STAR registry gives year constructed 2022 for both Shellhorn DC1 and DC2, which disagrees with DCF for DC1.

site_name: Yondr Loudoun County campus, 24171 Youngwood Ln, Aldie, VA 20105
year_evidence_quote: has completed its first 48MW data center in Loudoun County, Northern Virginia,
year_site_match: Yondr's own press release, datelined 'Loudoun County, VA., – November 18, 2024', titled 'Yondr Group's first Northern Virginia data center is ready for service', describes the first 48MW building of its '96MW two-building campus' built 'in partnership with JK Land Holdings, LLC (JKLH)'. It is tied to the record by operator, county, and the fact that it is Yondr's first Northern Virginia data center. No page I opened gives a street address, Aldie, or Youngwood Ln; the address tie is NOT confirmed from a non-directory page.
verification: I replaced the cited W.Media article with the operator's own dated release, which is stronger: on Nov. 18, 2024 Yondr said it 'has completed its first 48MW data center in Loudoun County' and 'Yondr has delivered the completed data center within two years of breaking ground in 2022', with a quoted 'handover' of the first tranche of capacity. The Dec. 17, 2025 Yondr release and W.Media (Dec. 22, 2025) both confirm completion of building 1 and first 12MW ready-for-service on building 2. The year 2024 for the campus's first building would be high on the statement alone; I marked medium because the street address is unconfirmed and one loose end exists: a June 24, 2026 Yondr release says issuer 'Yondr JK 1, LLC' will fund a 48 MW data center 'to be built on an approximately 14.3-acre property in Loudoun County, Virginia'. I am uncertain whether that is the campus's second building or a separate parcel, and the record's permittee (per the researcher's note, 'Yondr JK 2 LLC', which I did not see on any page) could be either entity. If the Youngwood Ln permit turns out to be a separate later parcel, 2024 would not apply. Yondr's Aug. 2026 72MW site is in Manassas and is a different project. Primary operating evidence is 'completed/ready for service/handover', not a statement that tenant load is live.

lead.year_evidence_quote: Yondr completed the first 48 MW data center at the Loudoun County campus in 2024.

phases.label: Building 2, first ready-for-service phase (12 MW of 48 MW)

lead.notes: W.Media (Dec. 22, 2025) says Yondr completed the first 48 MW data center on its Loudoun County campus in 2024, and that the first 12 MW phase of the second 48 MW building is ready for service, with full operations expected in 2026. The article gives no street address. The Youngwood Ln address comes only from directories, and I know of no other Yondr campus in Loudoun, hence medium. The permittee 'Yondr JK 2 LLC' may be the second building's entity (a June 2026 article names 'Yondr JK 1'), but the campus's first building dates to 2024.

Opening year as stated by the press is 2009.
